dimensions.assessment: Affects all minor users of social media platforms under 17, their parents, social media platform providers, and app stores nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: To protect minors from harms associated with ephemeral messaging features and unsolicited direct contact on social media platforms

dimensions.assessment: Significantly alters how minor accounts interact on social media by banning certain messaging features by default, requiring parental controls, and mandating verifiable parental consent.
dimensions.evidence: A provider of a social media platform may not offer, provide, or enable any ephemeral messaging feature of such social media platform to any covered user

dimensions.assessment: Relies on existing Federal Trade Commission and state enforcement mechanisms without specifying new federal appropriations.

Establishes a broad federal regulatory framework preempting state laws, creating new technical compliance mandates for tech platforms and app stores, and granting enforcement powers to the FTC and state attorneys general.
dimensions.evidence: A violation of this Act shall be treated as a violation of a regulation under 18(a)(1)(B) of the Federal Trade Commission Act

dimensions.assessment: Permanent federal regulatory standard with phased implementation deadlines ranging from 180 days to 18 months post-enactment.
dimensions.evidence: this Act shall take effect on the date that is 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Specific technical standards for verifying parental consent or costs of compliance for platforms are not detailed.
importance_detail.rationale: Imposes sweeping new federal requirements on social media platforms regarding ephemeral messaging for minors, parental direct messaging controls, default messaging restrictions for users under 13, and app store warnings, backed by FTC and state attorney general enforcement.

label: H.R. 6257

latest_action.text: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Safe Messaging for Kids Act of 2025 protects minors (individuals under 17) on social media platforms by banning ephemeral messaging features for them and requiring parental direct messaging controls. Social media companies must give parents tools to manage direct messaging requests, approve or deny contacts, disable messaging, and automatically turn off direct messaging by default for users under 13. App stores must also provide warnings under certain conditions. The Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general enforce the law, and state-level laws on the subject are preempted.

affected_groups.effect: Prohibited from using ephemeral messaging features on social media platforms, and subject to parental controls and default messaging restrictions on direct messaging.
Provided with tools, portals, notifications, and settings to monitor, approve, deny, or disable direct messaging features for minor users under their legal custody.
Required to update platform designs to remove ephemeral messaging for minors, implement parental control interfaces, set default messaging restrictions for users under 13, and prevent circumvention.
Required to provide warnings to parents when minors attempt to download or purchase apps with direct messaging features under specific parental settings.
Empowered to enforce the Act, investigate violations, and bring civil actions or seek penalties.
affected_groups.group: Federal Trade Commission and State Attorneys General

key_provisions: Prohibits social media platforms from offering, providing, or enabling ephemeral (disappearing) messaging features to any minor user under 17.
Mandates that social media platforms provide easily accessible and usable parental direct messaging controls requiring verifiable parental consent.
Sets default settings so that direct messaging features are completely disabled for any minor user under 13 unless a parent provides verifiable parental consent to enable them.

Gives parents default abilities to receive timely notifications and approve or deny direct messaging requests from unapproved contacts, view and manage approved contacts, be notified of profile age changes, and disable direct messaging entirely.

Requires app store providers to give a clear and conspicuous warning to parents when a minor attempts to download or purchase an app with a direct messaging feature, if the parent has required parental consent for downloads.
Enforces violations of the Act through the Federal Trade Commission as unfair or deceptive acts or practices, and authorizes State attorneys general to bring civil actions.
Specifies that the Act does not require weakening, impairing, decrypting, or undermining end-to-end encryption or other security controls.
missing_information: The specific financial costs or budget allocations for enforcement by the Federal Trade Commission and state governments.
The exact monetary penalty amounts for violations, though they fall under the standard penalties of the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Social media companies must give parents tools to manage direct messaging requests, approve or deny contacts, disable messaging, and automatically turn off direct messaging by default for users under 13. summary_detail.significance: The bill introduces targeted federal rules governing specific communication features and parental consent mechanisms on social media for all minor users nationwide, preempting state-level laws on the same subject.
